novum_candidates.description: Old Matthew Bennett's delusion that he is the King of England (and generally that he holds royal authority), which governs the household's social logic and blocks Katie's marriage.

novelty.rationale: The grandfather's belief that he is King of England is a psychological delusion of a senile old man, not a totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical norm. The story world remains ordinary contemporary New York; nothing in the storyworld is actually changed. Characters explicitly recognize it as 'all nonsense.' There is no alteration to the universe, only one man's private false belief.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The delusion is presented as ordinary age-related dementia, not as any systematic imaginary science or alternative social organization. It has no immanent coherent logic that reorganizes the world; it is simply a recurring, shifting mental confusion (President Roosevelt, Prophet Elijah, King of England).

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The delusion drives the central conflict: because the grandfather believes he is king, he forbids his 'granddaughter of the King of England' from marrying a commoner, and the entire plot revolves around resolving this obstacle. However, this narrative centrality does not make it a novum, since it lacks novelty and cognitive validation.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The reader-facing contrast is between the shared knowledge that the belief is false and the old man's sincere conviction; this is dramatic irony arising from a mundane delusion rather than a cognitively estranging novum. The storyworld remains the empirical norm.

novum_candidates.description: The 'King of Coney Island' title won by popular vote in an annual Mardi Gras election, which Ted uses to present himself as royalty and secure permission to marry.

novelty.rationale: The Coney Island Mardi Gras king is an actual festival custom of the empirical world, a ceremonial popularity title, not a world-altering difference. It introduces no change to the story universe.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The election mechanism is mundane and real; there is no imaginary scientific or social system to validate as a novum, so the dimension is not meaningfully applicable.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The Coney Island kingship provides the plot resolution: Ted exploits the grandfather's unfamiliarity with Coney Island to claim a 'royal alliance.' Yet this is an ordinary device, not a novum.

novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: Any estrangement here is comedic, based on the old man's ignorance of a real place, not on cognitive novelty. This is a mundane social custom, not a novum.
